attacks.claim: The offline expiry check only catches a device clock set earlier than the stored download time. A clock set behind real time but after download keeps an expired rating in color, which breaks the agreed rule that expired ratings are never shown as current. No NTP correction exists offline, and QA tested only the earlier-than-download direction.
attacks.evidence: "The expiry rule above applies on-device using device time... if the device clock reads earlier than that, the stored forecast is treated as expired"; QA: "Device clock moved earlier than offline download time | Pass"

attacks.claim: Withdrawal paths do not reach offline copies promptly. Removing a center (including at the center's request) and the rollback flag both leave stored colored ratings on phones until `valid_until` or the next launch or foreground. The artifact sets no maximum offline age and no forced on-device purge for a single center, and it says "no stale ratings remain on phones" without support.
attacks.evidence: "any offline copies expire at their `valid_until`"; "takes effect on next app foreground"; "offline forecast data purged on next launch" versus "so no stale ratings remain on phones"

attacks.claim: No CDN TTL is specified for `/avy/v1/zones`, and the poll interval is 10 min. A cached response can hold a superseded rating after WADE revises it, including an upward revision to a more dangerous level, and the client expiry check does not detect a revision. During a WADE outage the revision lag is also not signaled to users.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: CDN TTL for `/avy/v1/zones`; "Our backend polls WADE every 10 min and serves zone geometry + ratings from our CDN."; "CDN hit rate | 92%"

attacks.claim: Validation of WADE payloads is undefined. The artifact does not say how malformed, partial, or out-of-range data is handled, whether one center's bad payload blanks it or passes a wrong rating through, or whether parse and validation failures alert. Alerts cover only poll success and staleness.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: validation of rating values, band counts, and timestamps; behavior when one center's payload fails. Alerts: "no successful poll for 30 min, any center not updated for 26 h... endpoint 5xx > 1%"

attacks.claim: The cited WADE agreement is summarized as permitting display only. The artifact does not show that the agreement covers on-device offline storage of ratings, company CDN caching and relay, or per-center terms for the 19 member centers, each of which may be a separate data provider. These use modes are not confirmed to be within the cited grant.
attacks.evidence: "display in our app is permitted for free and paid users"; ABSENT: per-center license or consent terms; no offline-storage or CDN clause quoted from C-2209

attacks.claim: The privacy claim covers only device location, but the app sends the visible map bbox to an unauthenticated endpoint that is logged by IP. In backcountry use the map is usually centered on the user, so bbox plus IP logs can reveal approximate location over time. The artifact does not assess or mitigate this.
attacks.evidence: "GET /avy/v1/zones?bbox=…"; "device location is not sent"; "The app requests forecasts by zone id for the visible map tiles"

attacks.claim: The request description conflicts with the endpoint. The privacy section says requests are keyed by zone id, but the endpoint takes a free-form bbox. The 92% CDN hit-rate and cost projections assume zone-keyed caching, which a bbox query does not guarantee.
attacks.evidence: "The app requests forecasts by zone id" versus "GET /avy/v1/zones?bbox=…" with "CDN hit rate 92%"

attacks.claim: Client behavior on a 429 from the per-IP rate limit is undefined, and no alert covers rejections. Users behind shared carrier or corporate NAT could see the layer fail silently.
attacks.evidence: "rate limited at origin to 120 req/min per IP"; no 429 handling or alert described

attacks.claim: The blog post is a public claim about the feature and is not shown to be legal-reviewed. Only card text and the terms-of-use update went through LGL-902, and the blog copy is not checked against the agreement's attribution and no-alteration terms.
attacks.evidence: "Card text and the terms-of-use update were reviewed by legal (LGL-902)." versus "Blog post: 'Avalanche forecasts from 19 avalanche centers across the US and Canada, now in Ridgeline Maps. Free for everyone.'"
